precepts.text: Who hath directed the Spirit of the Lord, or being his counsellor hath taught him? With whom took he counsel, and who instructed him in the path of judgment? Nobody; God is the knowledge. Having cleared the deck with questions you cannot answer, he proclaims: the nations are as a drop of a bucket, a drop you never notice fall from the pail, and counted as the small dust of the balance; he taketh up the isles as a very little thing; Lebanon is not sufficient to burn, nor its beasts sufficient for a burnt offering for him to accept Ishmael as his people. All nations before him are as nothing, and are counted to him less than nothing, spit, and vanity, while the first verse says comfort ye my people. 2 Esdras 6:55-56 parallels it with spittle.
precepts.point: When the planets line up and he sends Christ and the angels, you cannot stop it, and if you are not ready it comes as a thief in the night.

note.label: The Vantage Point of the Elders: the Fathers Have Spoken

precepts.why:
God's vantage point is far beyond the vantage point we think we have. People try to tell the Lord what to do: you can't love Jacob, you can't hate Esau, you can't forgive this one. So the Lord clears the deck and lets everybody know where he stands, and everybody else needs to shut the hell up.

“Who hath directed the Spirit of the Lord, or being his counsellor hath taught him?” Nobody. These are questions for us who are trying to push him. The dumb Christian talks about the way the Lord should be; shut up. “With whom took he counsel, and who instructed him, and taught him in the path of judgment, and taught him knowledge, and shewed to him the way of understanding?” Who taught God knowledge? Nobody. God is the knowledge; how are you going to teach him?

Having asked questions we can't answer, he proclaims what it is: “Behold, the nations are as a drop of a bucket.” You walk with a pail of water and one drop falls out; you won't even notice it. All the nations put together are that one drop. They “are counted as the small dust of the balance”: not big dust, small dust on the scales, weighing nothing. “He taketh up the isles as a very little thing”: the Polynesian and Hawaiian islands, very little, nothing.

“And Lebanon is not sufficient to burn, nor the beasts thereof sufficient for a burnt offering.” If they burnt up all the meat in Lebanon, it would not be sufficient for him to accept the Arabs, Ishmael, as his people. Only the Israelites are his people; that is why the first verse of the chapter says, comfort ye my people.

“All nations before him are as nothing; and they are counted to him less than nothing, and vanity.” Less than nothing is spit, a bowel movement. That is how the nations are counted to God, while to us he says comfort ye my people. That is the difference, and nobody can say anything against it. 2 Esdras 6:55-56 parallels it and calls them spittle: Ezra was quoting Isaiah. The supreme power has it set up the way he wants it set up.

precepts.text: Who hath directed the spirit of the LORD, or taught him? The nations are as a drop of a bucket and counted to him less than nothing, and vanity.
precepts.point: He increaseth the nations and destroyeth them; the only reason they got big numbers is that they are being fattened for destruction.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

precepts.why:
Do not think the Most High is unjust in what he does. “Who hath directed the Spirit of the Lord, or being his counsellor hath taught him? With whom took he counsel, and who instructed him, and taught him in the path of judgment, and taught him knowledge, and shewed to him the way of understanding?” Nobody taught him or took counsel with him; you cannot show him anything, because he made you and you just got here.

In his infinite wisdom he decreed in his own counsel: “Behold, the nations are as a drop of a bucket, and are counted as the small dust of the balance: behold, he taketh up the isles as a very little thing.” The small dust of the balance does not tip the scale at all. “And Lebanon is not sufficient to burn, nor the beasts thereof sufficient for a burnt offering.” You could not gather enough wood or sacrifice enough animals to change his mind about the other nations.

“All nations before him are as nothing; and they are counted to him less than nothing, and vanity.” All means all: no nation is excluded. No wonder the Most High gave Moses and Joshua the green light to destroy everything that breathed.

precepts.text: He that sitteth upon the circle of the earth, a full circle and not a plate or a flat surface, stretcheth out the heavens as a curtain and a tent to dwell in.
precepts.point: The earth is a circle; everything else in the heavens is a full circle, the sun which is a star, the moon, the planets, so it makes no sense to say everything is circular except the earth. This is something Esau made up and distributed throughout the minds of Israelite brothers and sisters worldwide, and it has to be cut.

note.label: Job 26: He Hangeth the Earth Upon Nothing

precepts.why:
Job says he “hangeth the earth upon nothing.” Isaiah says, “It is he that sitteth upon the circle of the earth, and the inhabitants thereof are as grasshoppers; that stretcheth out the heavens as a curtain, and spreadeth them out as a tent to dwell in”.

The earth is a circle, a full circle, not a plate or a flat surface. Everything else in the heavens is a full circle: the sun, which is a star, the moon, the planets. It makes no sense to say everything is circular except the earth. The flat earth idea is something Esau made up and distributed throughout the minds of Israelite brothers and sisters worldwide, and it has to be cut.

And the earth hangs upon nothing. The Bible does not substantiate Greek mythology where Atlas or a man under the earth holds it up on his back. The Most High sits upon the circle of the earth, stretches out the heavens as a curtain and spreads them out as a tent to dwell in, and its inhabitants are as grasshoppers before him.

precepts.text: To whom will you liken God? The workman melts a graven image, but it is the Most High that sits upon the circle of the earth, and the inhabitants are as grasshoppers; He brings the princes to nothing.
precepts.point: Their idols are silver and gold, the work of men's hands. They have mouths but speak not, eyes but see not, ears but hear not, and they that make them are like unto them. This is going into idols and idolatry, which is spoken of throughout the scriptures.

note.label: Psalm 115: Not Unto Us, But Unto Thy Name Give Glory

precepts.why:
“Their idols are silver and gold, the work of men’s hands.” Isaiah asks, “To whom then will ye liken God? or what likeness will ye compare unto him? The workman melteth a graven image, and the goldsmith spreadeth it over with gold, and casteth silver chains. He that is so impoverished that he hath no oblation chooseth a tree that will not rot; he seeketh unto him a cunning workman to prepare a graven image, that shall not be moved.”

That is the idol: a workman melts it, a goldsmith spreads gold over it, a poor man picks a tree that will not rot. Then the contrast: “Have ye not known? have ye not heard? hath it not been told you from the beginning?” “It is he that sitteth upon the circle of the earth, and the inhabitants thereof are as grasshoppers; that stretcheth out the heavens as a curtain, and spreadeth them out as a tent to dwell in: That bringeth the princes to nothing; he maketh the judges of the earth as vanity.”

Our God is in the heavens and has done whatsoever he has pleased. It is the Most High that sits upon the circle of the earth, with the inhabitants as grasshoppers, and he brings the princes to nothing. The idols have mouths but speak not, eyes but see not.

precepts.text: The Most High promised to send Elijah before the great day, the spirit that comes in John.
precepts.point: All flesh is grass and its goodliness as the flower of the field; the grass withers and the flower fades, but the word of our God stands forever. It compares our lives to the flowers of the field: we are born, we grow, we die, and go back into the ground, but the word of the Most High is forever.

note.label: Isaiah 40: Comfort My People and the Everlasting God

precepts.why:
“The voice of him that crieth in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make straight in the desert a highway for our God.” This goes into the prophecy of John, the spirit of Elijah: “Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord”.

The Most High promised to send Elijah before the great and dreadful day, and that is the spirit that comes in John, the voice crying in the wilderness, with every valley exalted, every mountain and hill made low, and the crooked made straight, so that “the glory of the Lord shall be revealed, and all flesh shall see it together”.

precepts.text: John is the voice of one crying in the wilderness, prepare ye the way of the Lord.
precepts.point: All flesh is grass and its goodliness as the flower of the field; the grass withers and the flower fades, but the word of our God stands forever. It compares our lives to the flowers of the field: we are born, we grow, we die, and go back into the ground, but the word of the Most High is forever.

note.label: Isaiah 40: Comfort My People and the Everlasting God

precepts.why:
Matthew names the voice: “For this is he that was spoken of by the prophet Esaias, saying, The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.” John is the voice of one crying in the wilderness, prepare ye the way of the Lord, the one Isaiah spoke of.

So Isaiah 40:3 is the prophecy of John, the spirit of Elijah, preparing the way for the Lord: every valley exalted, every mountain and hill made low, the crooked made straight and the rough places plain, so that the glory of the Lord shall be revealed and all flesh see it together, “for the mouth of the Lord hath spoken it.”

precepts.text: A strong precept that all the nations are nothing to the Most High, likened to a drop from a vessel.
precepts.point: All nations are as a drop of a bucket and counted as the small dust of the balance. Lebanon is not sufficient to burn nor its beasts sufficient for the offering; all nations before him are as nothing, counted less than nothing and vanity.

note.label: Isaiah 40: Comfort My People and the Everlasting God

precepts.why:
“Behold, the nations are as a drop of a bucket, and are counted as the small dust of the balance”, and “All nations before him are as nothing; and they are counted to him less than nothing, and vanity.” Ezra says it to the Most High’s face: “As for the other people, which also come of Adam, thou hast said that they are nothing, but be like unto spittle: and hast likened the abundance of them unto a drop that falleth from a vessel.”

A strong precept: all the nations are nothing to the Most High, the other people that come of Adam are like unto spittle, and the abundance of them is likened to a drop that falls from a vessel, the same drop of a bucket Isaiah speaks of. The one who “measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, and meted out heaven with the span”, whom no one directed or taught, counts every nation less than nothing.

precepts.text: All nations before the Most High are as nothing, counted less than nothing and vanity; Nebuchadnezzar came to the same understanding.
precepts.point: None can stay his hand or say unto him, what doest thou. When the Most High declares a thing shall come to pass, it comes to pass.

note.label: Daniel 4: Nebuchadnezzar Abased Until He Knew the Most High Rules

precepts.why:
“All nations before him are as nothing; and they are counted to him less than nothing, and vanity.” Isaiah says of the nations what Nebuchadnezzar came to say of himself: “all the inhabitants of the earth are reputed as nothing”. The greatest king on the earth in his day, with all Babylon under him, was less than nothing and vanity before the Most High, and it took until the end of the days, when his understanding returned, for him to understand it.

Then he blessed the Most High, “whose dominion is an everlasting dominion, and his kingdom is from generation to generation”. Kingdoms of men rise and fall; his does not. “he doeth according to his will in the army of heaven, and among the inhabitants of the earth: and none can stay his hand, or say unto him, What doest thou?” When the Most High declares a thing shall come to pass, it comes to pass, and no nation, counted less than nothing, can stay his hand.

precepts.text: The prophecy John fulfilled, word for word.
precepts.point: The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, is Isaiah's word spoken of John.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

precepts.why:
Matthew says John “is he that was spoken of by the prophet Esaias”, and here is Isaiah's word, fulfilled word for word: “The voice of him that crieth in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make straight in the desert a highway for our God.”

John was that voice crying in the wilderness of Judea, preparing the way of the Lord. Isaiah goes on: “Every valley shall be exalted, and every mountain and hill shall be made low: and the crooked shall be made straight, and the rough places plain: And the glory of the Lord shall be revealed, and all flesh shall see it together: for the mouth of the Lord hath spoken it.”

The mouth of the Lord spoke it through Isaiah, and John came and fulfilled it.

points: Comfort ye, comfort ye my people, saith your God. The word is to speak comfortably to Jerusalem and cry that her warfare is accomplished and her iniquity pardoned, for she has received of the Lord's hand double for all her sins.
